module_title: Major Amendments - Parts, Schedules, and Emergency Safeguards
introduction: At this level, we focus on the technical additions like new Parts and Schedules, and how the 44th Amendment made it harder for the government to declare a National Emergency.

core_concepts.title: 42nd Amendment: Technical Additions
core_concepts.description: Added Part IVA (Fundamental Duties - Art 51A) and Part XIVA (Administrative Tribunals). It also made the President 'bound' by the advice of the Cabinet.

core_concepts.title: 44th Amendment: Emergency Safeguards
core_concepts.description: Replaced the term 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' in Article 352. It mandated that the President can only declare Emergency on written advice of the Cabinet. It also ensured that Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an emergency.

core_concepts.title: 73rd Amendment: Part IX & 11th Schedule
core_concepts.description: Added Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and the 11th Schedule to the Constitution. The 11th Schedule contains 29 functional items for Panchayats.

core_concepts.title: 74th Amendment: Part IXA & 12th Schedule
core_concepts.description: Added Part IXA (Articles 243P to 243ZG) and the 12th Schedule. The 12th Schedule contains 18 functional items for Municipalities.

important_entities.name: Swaran Singh Committee (1976)
important_entities.significance: The 42nd Amendment's addition of Fundamental Duties was based on this committee's recommendations.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: While the 42nd made the President a rubber stamp, the 44th gave the President the power to send the advice back to the Cabinet 'once' for reconsideration.
The 73rd and 74th are '1992 Acts' but they came into force in 1993. 24th April (73rd) is celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Panchayats (11th Schedule) have 29 subjects. Municipalities (12th Schedule) have 18 subjects.

exam_strategy_tips: Note the shift in the term for National Emergency (352): Internal Disturbance -> Armed Rebellion (44th Amendment). This is a favorite of UPSC and State PCS.
Understand that the 42nd and 44th amendments are essentially 'Opposites' in their treatment of Executive power.
